exposure: Medical management (systemic methotrexate, local potassium chloride or methotrexate)
Other less frequently used treatment options
cohort: The study included 460 patients with live or failing cesarean scar pregnancies who received active treatment before 12+6 weeks' gestation and were registered in an international registry.
finding: Cesarean scar pregnancies can be effectively managed in the first trimester (over 90% success) with suction evacuation, balloon treatment, or surgical excision, with effectiveness decreasing as gestational age advances, while systemic methotrexate was found to be least effective.
